chapter: New Orleans bands, clubs and players
title: New Orleans musicians visiting Sweden and money for traditional players
summary: Few New Orleans bands tour Sweden, modern jazz is more popular, and traditional players earn little except on tours and in the country.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Have you had a lot of New Orleans musicians coming to Sweden?
Well, George Lewis is coming there quite often. Albert Nicholas, Edmund Hall, you know. Otherwise it's mostly Chris Bob and Papa Boo coming there. They'd very seldom bring in the-
Yeah. A lot of modern jazz of course. Very lot of modern jazz.
Yeah. It's very popular in Sweden. I guess it's more popular than any other country in Europe. I see. And there's also more modern jazz musicians in Sweden than in other countries.
Well, how do the traditional musicians make it then? They don't make it. They just play
You don't get much money or what?

No. We make- sometimes we make money like when I played at the jazz festival two years ago and we went- this Christmas we went on a tour to Denmark for 14 days with the band. Then we make some money. Otherwise we make money when we go out on the countryside. Not in Stockholm. In Stockholm you don't make no money at all no more. They all want modern jazz? Well they don't want pop music. Modern jazz they don't make it either. The jazz make it when they play in restaurants. They never play for dancing more than jazz. So. OK. OK.
